option_description: Whether the scrape target's /metrics endpoint requires authentication. node_exporter and most exporters serve /metrics with NO auth by default; the exporter-toolkit --web.config.file adds basic_auth_users (bcrypt) and/or tls_server_config so the endpoint is not anonymously readable.
security_impact: One of the OR-triggers for "Unauthenticated /metrics endpoint exposure" — firing when this is false (anonymous /metrics) — and contributes to "/metrics not network-restricted to the monitoring segment": an open endpoint that is also network-reachable is the full anonymous-exposure condition. Also frames the severity of "Sensitive data leaked in metric labels".

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the exporter's web.config.yml (path passed via --web.config.file) for an auth/TLS block.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: basic_auth_users: and/or tls_server_config: blocks present (secure); file absent or no auth block (insecure = open /metrics)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Curl the /metrics endpoint with no credentials and observe the HTTP status.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 401 (auth required, secure) vs 200 with metrics body returned to an unauthenticated request (insecure)

option_description: Whether the target /metrics endpoint is reachable only from the Prometheus monitoring segment (firewall/security-group/network-policy limiting ingress on the exporter port, e.g. 9100, to the monitoring server source). The Prometheus security model warns /metrics of instrumented binaries must not be exposed to public networks.
security_impact: Primary mitigation and OR-trigger interplay for "/metrics not network-restricted to the monitoring segment" and "Unauthenticated /metrics endpoint exposure" — firing when this is false (0.0.0.0 bind, no ingress filtering, internet-reachable). Also bounds the leak scope of "Sensitive data leaked in metric labels".

how_to_obtain.instruction: From OUTSIDE the monitoring segment, attempt to fetch the exporter port and confirm it is unreachable.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -sS -m5 http://<target>:9100/metrics  # run from OUTSIDE the monitoring segment
how_to_obtain.expected_output: connection refused/timeout from outside the monitoring segment (secure); metrics returned from an arbitrary host (insecure exposure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the firewall / security-group / network-policy ingress rules governing the exporter port.
how_to_obtain.command: Review firewall / security-group / network-policy rules governing the exporter port (e.g. 9100)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ingress to the exporter port limited to the Prometheus server source (secure); open/any-source ingress (insecure)

option_description: Whether the metric label values emitted on this scrape carry no secrets, credentials, internal hostnames/IPs, build/version, process/environment data, or accidentally-labelled tokens. The Prometheus security model assumes /metrics readers are untrusted.
security_impact: Primary OR-trigger for "Sensitive data leaked in metric labels" — firing when this is false, i.e. sensitive data IS present in labels on a reachable /metrics endpoint, a direct confidentiality breach. Also frames the severity of "Unauthenticated /metrics endpoint exposure".

how_to_obtain.instruction: Curl /metrics and grep label values for secret-bearing or internal-address patterns.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: no secret-bearing or internal-address labels returned (secure); credentials/internal IPs/hostnames present in labels (insecure exposure)

option_description: Whether a label-scrubbing / masking control (metric_relabel_configs labeldrop/labelkeep, exporter-side redaction, or instrumentation that excludes secret/host fields) is applied so sensitive values cannot reach exported labels.
security_impact: Secondary OR-trigger reinforcing "Sensitive data leaked in metric labels" — firing when this is false (no scrubbing in place, so sensitive label values flow to readers).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review metric_relabel_configs for labeldrop/labelkeep rules and any exporter-side redaction.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: labeldrop/labelkeep (or exporter redaction) dropping secret/host label keys before ingest (secure); no scrubbing rules present (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: After confirming masking config, curl /metrics and verify the targeted secret/host label keys are absent from the emitted series.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: the intended-to-be-masked label keys do not appear (masking effective); they still appear (masking absent/ineffective)

option_description: Whether data-minimization is enforced for what this flow exports — only operationally necessary metrics/labels are emitted, reducing the surface for accidental sensitive-value inclusion. Supporting context, not itself a trigger.
security_impact: Supporting context for "Sensitive data leaked in metric labels" — it is not itself a condition trigger, but a minimized export set reduces the surface that the leak trigger evaluates.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Curl /metrics and review the emitted metric/label set against operational need.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: only operationally necessary counters/gauges emitted; high-cardinality or descriptive labels carrying environment data are NOT exported (secure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm a review process exists that limits exported metrics/labels to operational need.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: documented minimization of the exported metric/label set; no descriptive environment data labelled (secure)

option_description: Whether the scrape config bounds per-target ingest volume: sample_limit, label_limit, label_name_length_limit, label_value_length_limit and target_limit set to finite non-zero values. These all default to 0/unset, meaning Prometheus trusts whatever cardinality and label volume the target returns.
security_impact: Primary OR-trigger for "Cardinality bomb / TSDB resource exhaustion" — firing when this is false: a malicious target ships millions of high-cardinality series or oversized labels and exhausts/OOMs the TSDB.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect prometheus.yml scrape_configs[] for the cardinality/label limit keys set to finite non-zero values.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: finite non-zero values present (secure); keys absent / 0 = unbounded, target-trusted (insecure)

option_description: Whether scrape_config.body_size_limit is set to a finite non-zero value capping the size of the response body Prometheus will read from a target. It defaults to 0 (no limit), so a malicious target can return an arbitrarily large /metrics body and exhaust scraper memory before any per-sample limit applies.
security_impact: Primary OR-trigger for "Cardinality bomb / TSDB resource exhaustion" — firing when this is false (unbounded body accepted from an untrusted target), exhausting scraper memory ahead of any per-sample limit.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect prometheus.yml scrape_configs[].body_size_limit for a finite non-zero value (e.g. 10MB).
how_to_obtain.expected_output: body_size_limit set to a finite non-zero value such as 10MB (secure); key absent / 0 = unbounded body accepted (insecure)

option_description: Whether write access to scrape_config (prometheus.yml), file_sd target files, and relabel_configs that build target addresses is limited to trusted operators, and SD-derived targets are validated/allowlisted. When unrestricted, any party able to edit scrape config or relabel rules can point Prometheus at arbitrary internal URLs.
security_impact: OR-trigger for "SSRF via editable scrape config / service discovery" — firing on the insecure (unrestricted) state, where editable config/relabel rules let an attacker steer Prometheus at internal targets.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review who can write prometheus.yml, file_sd target files, and the http_sd backing service, plus relabel_configs that build target addresses from SD labels.
how_to_obtain.command: Review who can write prometheus.yml, file_sd target files, and http_sd backing service; review relabel_configs that build target addresses from SD labels
how_to_obtain.expected_output: write access to config + SD sources limited to trusted operators; SD-derived targets validated/allowlisted (secure); any service-discovery contributor can inject targets (insecure SSRF surface)

option_description: Whether the service-discovery backends feeding scrape targets (http_sd endpoint, file_sd files, Consul, etc.) are trusted and write-restricted so untrusted parties cannot inject arbitrary target addresses. When untrusted, an attacker who can mutate SD data controls what Prometheus fetches.
security_impact: OR-trigger for "SSRF via editable scrape config / service discovery" — firing on the insecure (untrusted SD) state, where an attacker mutating SD data dictates Prometheus's fetch targets.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Identify the SD backends in use and confirm write access to each is authenticated and restricted to trusted parties with target addresses validated/allowlisted.
how_to_obtain.command: Review who can write prometheus.yml, file_sd target files, and http_sd backing service; review relabel_configs that build target addresses from SD labels
how_to_obtain.expected_output: write access to config + SD sources limited to trusted operators; SD-derived targets validated/allowlisted (secure); any service-discovery contributor can inject targets (insecure SSRF surface)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Enumerate the SD source types configured for this job (http_sd, file_sd, Consul, etc.) to scope the trust review.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: the set of SD backends feeding targets, each then checked for write-restriction/allowlisting

option_description: Whether proxying exporters (Blackbox/SNMP) restrict the targets they will probe to a validated allowlist, so they cannot be coerced into requesting arbitrary internal endpoints and leaking client-side basic_auth secrets. When absent, the proxying exporter is an open SSRF relay.
security_impact: OR-trigger for "SSRF via editable scrape config / service discovery" — firing on the insecure (no allowlist) state, where a Blackbox/SNMP proxy can be aimed at arbitrary internal endpoints and leak presented credentials.

how_to_obtain.instruction: If Blackbox/SNMP or other proxying exporters are in use, confirm the target parameter is constrained to a validated allowlist rather than accepting any caller-supplied address.
how_to_obtain.command: Review who can write prometheus.yml, file_sd target files, and http_sd backing service; review relabel_configs that build target addresses from SD labels
how_to_obtain.expected_output: proxying-exporter target constrained to a validated allowlist (secure); any caller-supplied address accepted = open SSRF relay (insecure)

option_description: Whether the Prometheus scrape_config.scheme is https for this flow. scheme defaults to 'http' (plaintext); scraping over http exposes the often sensitive-labelled metrics and any basic_auth credential the scraper presents on the wire.
security_impact: OR-trigger for "Plaintext scrape transport" — firing (is_false) when the scrape runs over plaintext http, exposing metrics and presented credentials to an adjacent sniffer.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect prometheus.yml scrape_configs[].scheme for this job.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: scheme: https (secure); scheme: http or key absent = default http (insecure)

option_description: Shared workspace attestation that this flow's transport is encrypted end to end — both the client-side scheme (https) and the exporter serving /metrics under tls_server_config, neither plaintext push nor plaintext exporter response.
security_impact: OR-trigger for "Plaintext scrape transport" — firing (is_false) when any leg of the scrape is carried in cleartext, exposing metrics and presented basic_auth credentials to an adjacent sniffer.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm the exporter serves /metrics under TLS by checking web.config.yml for a tls_server_config block.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: tls_server_config with cert_file/key_file present (secure server leg); block absent = plaintext (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Capture traffic on the scrape port to verify no cleartext metrics body crosses the wire on either leg.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s http://<target>:9100/metrics | head  # expect refused/empty if TLS-only; cleartext body = insecure
how_to_obtain.expected_output: no cleartext metrics body observable (both legs TLS, secure); a readable plaintext metrics body (insecure leg)

option_description: The minimum negotiated TLS version for this flow — the exporter-toolkit tls_server_config.min_version on the server side and the scrape tls_config on the client side. Secure floor is TLS1.2 or TLS1.3.
security_impact: OR-trigger for "Plaintext scrape transport" — firing when the negotiated floor is in {SSLv3, TLS1.0, TLS1.1}, which permits downgrade/weak-cipher transport even when TLS is nominally present, leaving the scrape sniffable.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect web.config.yml tls_server_config.min_version (exporter) and the scrape tls_config (client) for the configured floor.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: tls_server_config with min_version: TLS12 (or TLS13) (secure); block absent = plaintext, or min_version below TLS12 (insecure)

how_to_obtain.instruction: Probe the exporter with a deprecated TLS version and confirm the handshake is refused.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: handshake failure for TLS1.1 (secure floor) vs successful negotiation of TLS1.1/older (insecure)

option_description: Whether Prometheus validates the scrape target's server certificate on the HTTPS scrape. Secure when scrape_config.tls_config.insecure_skip_verify is false (its default) with a ca_file pinning the trusted CA. When validation is disabled, a MITM can impersonate the target over a secure-looking HTTPS scrape.
security_impact: OR-trigger for "Unverified target TLS (insecure_skip_verify / MITM)" — firing when this is false (insecure_skip_verify: true / no trust anchor), letting a man-in-the-middle serve poisoned metrics or capture presented basic_auth/bearer credentials.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect prometheus.yml scrape_configs[].tls_config for insecure_skip_verify and ca_file.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: insecure_skip_verify: false (or absent) with ca_file present (secure); insecure_skip_verify: true (insecure)
